# Autocorrelation (lag 3) (`autocorrelation_lag3`)

*Category: Serial dependence & smoothing · Nature: estimated · Unit: correlation · Formula id: `autocorrelation_lag3@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Correlation between each return and the return 3 period(s) earlier.

## 2. Formula

```text
rho_3 = sum_(t>3) (r_t - m)(r_(t-3) - m) / sum_t (r_t - m)^2
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Context dependent.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

Whether good or bad periods tend to be followed by similar periods. Values near zero are typical for liquid, market-priced investments.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Sample autocorrelation (full-sample variance denominator). Significant positive low-lag autocorrelation is a hallmark of return smoothing or illiquidity (Getmansky, Lo & Makarov, 2004) and biases square-root-of-time annualization. Approximate 95% significance bound: +/- 1.96 / sqrt(n).

## 7. Assumptions

- Stationary returns.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Samples are short: standard error is roughly 1/sqrt(n).
- Volatility regimes change over the history.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 5 observations; low confidence below 36, moderate below 60. (policy `autocorrelation`: Requires at least 5 observations; standard error is roughly 1/sqrt(n), so low confidence below 36 and moderate below 60 observations.)

## 11. Sources

- Getmansky, M., Lo, A. W., & Makarov, I. (2004). An Econometric Model of Serial Correlation and Illiquidity in Hedge Fund Returns. Journal of Financial Economics, 74(3), 529-609.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Standard biased-denominator estimator; not bias-corrected.
